transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because my body just feels completely drained. It's like... it takes everything I have just to do basic things. Even walking from my car into the clinic today was just exhausting. And at work—I work in healthcare support—just sitting there and opening the EHR on the computer takes all the energy I've got. I just have nothing left.
Have you been feeling sad, down, or depressed lately?

Yeah, I really have. After all that energy I had just... dropped, I started feeling completely empty. Just hopeless most days. Honestly, it feels like I've already ruined my future in healthcare, and it hasn't even really started yet.
How long have you been feeling this way?

It's been about nine months. The depressed, guilty, and just completely exhausted part... it's lasted about nine months now, ever since I crashed after that really high-energy period I had before this.
During that high-energy period, did you need much less sleep than usual while still feeling rested?

Yeah. For a while back then, I could sleep for only two or three hours a night and still feel completely wired. I didn't need more than that. But lately... it's completely different. Now I either wake up way before dawn feeling just sick with worry, or I end up sleeping half the day and I still feel exhausted when I finally get up.
How long did that high-energy period last?

It lasted about two months, I think. The whole crisis kind of built up over that time, right after the clinic where I work changed my responsibilities. It just went on for those two months before I finally crashed.
During that high-energy period, were you ever hospitalized because of your mood or behavior?
No, I wasn't. Um... I didn't go to the hospital or get admitted or anything like that. I just kind of kept going until I finally crashed.
During that high-energy period, did you feel unusually elevated or irritable most of the day?

Yeah, both, actually. Some days I felt... just amazing, like I was completely unstoppable. But then, if someone at the clinic corrected my documentation, or told me I needed to slow down, I would just snap at them. I'd get really mad, like they were insulting me or something.
During that high-energy period, did your mood or behavior cause serious problems in your work or relationships?

Yeah, it definitely did. It got to the point where I just... I couldn't finish my documentation safely, and I couldn't stay focused on my patient-support tasks. It got so bad that employee health actually pulled me from work and sent me out for an emergency evaluation. And, um, I also had to stop preparing for my CNA certification. I just couldn't keep up with studying for it seriously anymore with everything going on.
During that high-energy period, did you hear or see things that others could not, or strongly believe things that others said were not true?

Yeah, I did. Um, I really believed I had this special medical mission. I also started hearing things... like, I would hear my name, or I thought the monitors at the clinic were actually calling out to me. 

But all of that—the ideas about the mission and hearing the monitors—that only happened when I was really wired, barely sleeping, and trying to completely overhaul the clinic. Once that whole high-energy period ended, I wasn't hearing those things anymore, and I didn't feel like I was chosen for anything.
Are you currently hearing or seeing things that others do not, or holding beliefs that others say are not true?

No, not right now. I don't hear anything out of the ordinary anymore, and I don't have those thoughts about a special mission or anything like that. It all went away after that really intense period stopped. Everything is just back to normal as far as that goes.
